releases.notes:
# Release Notes

## 0.2.0 – OG's QOL Meteor Addon

Minecraft 26.2 · Fabric Loader 0.19.3 · Meteor Client 26.2-SNAPSHOT · JDK 25

This release renames the project to **OG's QOL Meteor Addon** and merges the Litematica printer (previously released as
*SchemaForge* 0.1.0) and the standalone *Book Enchanter* addon into a single jar.

### Breaking changes

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Jar | `schemaforge-<version>.jar`, `book-enchanter-<version>.jar` | `og-qol-meteor-addon-<version>.jar` |
| Fabric mod ID | `schemaforge`, `book-enchanter` | `og-qol-meteor-addon` |
| Chat command | `.sf <sub>` | `.qol <sub>` (`.sf` stays as an alias) |
| Meteor categories | *SchemaForge*, *Book Enchanter* | *OG's QOL Printer*, *OG's QOL Enchanting* |
| HUD group | *SchemaForge* | *OG's QOL* |
| Data folder | `meteor-client/schemaforge/` | `meteor-client/og-qol/` (migrated automatically) |
| Repository | `github.com/Papxx/schemaforge` | `github.com/Papxx/og-qol-meteor-addon` (GitHub redirects the old URL) |
| Java package | `dev.tore.schemaforge` | `dev.tore.ogqol` (only matters for code that depends on the addon) |

**Upgrading:** remove the old `schemaforge` and `book-enchanter` jars from `mods` before adding the new one. Only one
of them may be installed, because they register the same module names.

### New

- **Book enchanter** (`auto-book-enchant`): rerolls an enchanting table until a chosen enchantment is offered on a
  book, with a toggle and minimum-level slider for each of the 36 table enchantments, bookshelf prediction from the
  server-sent seed, reroll and hit limits, and handling for books that hit nothing. It needs only Meteor Client.
- **Automatic data migration**: on the first start, the old `schemaforge` data folder (build checkpoints, undo logs,
  container indices) is renamed to `og-qol`. If the new folder already exists, neither folder is touched and a warning
  is logged, so no data is overwritten.

### Unchanged

- Module names (`schema-printer`, `container-restock`, `build-resume`, `auto-book-enchant`) and HUD element name
  (`build-progress`) are the same, so Meteor keeps all module settings and HUD layouts.
- All printer behaviour, settings and defaults are identical to SchemaForge 0.1.0, including additive-only by default
  and packet pacing through the per-tick budget.

### Diagnostics

A full audit ran before the rebrand:

- The build (`./gradlew build --rerun-tasks`) compiled with `-Xlint:deprecation -Xlint:unchecked` and gave **no
  compiler warnings or errors**.
- **All 431 unit tests passed**, with 0 failures and 0 skipped.
- No open `TODO`/`FIXME` markers were found in the sources.

The audit found no defects in the code, so this release contains no bug fixes. The only build-time warning comes from a
third-party library (JOML calls `sun.misc.Unsafe` on JDK 25). It is outside this project and does not affect behaviour.

### Validation

After the rename:

- `./gradlew build --rerun-tasks`: **successful**, with no compiler warnings.
- Unit tests: **431 / 431 passing** (printer planner, solver, restock, undo, checkpointing, signature checks, book
  enchanter offer evaluation and enchantment table data).
- The packaged jar was inspected: `fabric.mod.json` has the new ID, entry point `dev.tore.ogqol.OgQolAddon`, mixin
  config `ogqol.mixins.json` and icon path, and all of them resolve inside the jar.
- A search of all tracked files finds no remaining references to the old name, apart from the legacy folder name the
  migration needs and the upgrade notes.

**Not yet verified in-game:** loading the renamed jar in a real client, the data-folder migration and the book
enchanter at a live enchanting table. Please report any issues on the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/Papxx/og-qol-meteor-addon/issues).

releases.notes:
## SchemaForge 0.1.0 — first release (beta)

A Litematica printer for Meteor Client on Minecraft 26.2. It builds the placement you have
loaded in Litematica, walks between work areas with Baritone, and restocks from your chests.
It breaks nothing unless you allow it.

> **Beta.** 275 unit tests pass. Verified in-game: loading, `.sf doctor`, `.sf preview`,
> printing with Baritone navigation, safety pauses. **Not yet tried in-game:** container
> restock, `.sf undo`, fluids, rails, the FAST profile and accurate placement.
> Please report what breaks.

### What it does

- **Prints Litematica placements** — sub-regions, rotation and mirroring included. Works in
  small clusters, layer by layer, nearest-first, with up to three verify rounds.
- **Additive-only by default.** Wrong blocks are left alone and reported as *mismatched*;
  Baritone is not allowed to break anything during a run.
- **Correct orientation** for stairs, slabs, logs, furnaces, glazed terracotta, trapdoors,
  doors (hinge included), buttons, levers, torches, ladders, signs and rails.
- **Packet pacing** through a per-tick budget, in three profiles:
  - `VANILLA_LEGIT` (default) — one block per tick, real rotation
  - `FAST` — four per tick, spoofed rotation, warns in chat
  - `CUSTOM` — your own values
- **Baritone navigation** to clusters out of reach. Without Baritone it builds what it can reach.
- **Material restock.** Every chest, barrel, shulker and ender chest you open is remembered;
  `.sf scan` visits the ones nearby. When the printer runs dry it fetches what the next
  clusters need and comes back. Nothing is ever dropped. Shulkers from your inventory can be
  used too (off by default).
- **Safety pauses** on damage, low food, a player nearby, an unloaded chunk, or no material left.
- **Resume after a disconnect** with `.sf resume`, plus a progress HUD with percent,
  blocks per minute, ETA and missing items.
- **`.sf undo <n>`** removes the last blocks SchemaForge placed — only where the block is
  still exactly what it placed.

Optional, off by default: temporary dirt supports under floating blocks (needs additive-only
off), water and lava sources from a bucket, rail ordering (straight first, curves last), and
accurate placement that puts orientation into the click instead of turning the player when the
server speaks EasyPlace protocol V2 (Carpet) or V3 (Servux).

### Commands

`.sf doctor` · `.sf preview` · `.sf start` · `.sf pause` · `.sf resume` · `.sf stop` ·
`.sf status` · `.sf materials` · `.sf containers` · `.sf scan [radius]` · `.sf undo <n>`

See the [README](https://github.com/Papxx/schemaforge#readme) for every command and setting.

### Requirements

| | Version | |
|---|---|---|
| Minecraft | 26.2 | required |
| Fabric Loader | 0.19.3+ | required |
| Meteor Client | 26.2 snapshot | required |
| Litematica / MaLiLib | 0.28.8 / 0.29.6 (needs Fabric API) | needed for printing |
| Baritone (Meteor fork) | 26.2-SNAPSHOT | optional, for walking |

SchemaForge starts without Litematica or Baritone and tells you what is missing.

### Install

Drop `schemaforge-0.1.0.jar` into `mods/` next to Meteor Client, Litematica, MaLiLib and
Fabric API — plus Baritone if you want navigation. Start the game and run `.sf doctor`.

### Known limitations

- Only the first of several placements sharing a name can be selected.
- Blocks without a placement rule yet — redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, banners,
  plants, pressure plates, hanging signs, double slabs, opened doors, switched-on levers —
  are skipped and listed by `.sf preview`.
- `.sf scan` only finds containers in loaded chunks; `.sf undo` only reaches blocks near you.
- If a run stops mid-cluster, its temporary supports stay. They are logged, and `.sf undo`
  can remove them.
- Empty buckets are not refilled; every fluid source needs a full bucket.
- The ETA turns pessimistic after a long pause.
- Baritone may leave a harmless "client shutdown" crash report on quit. Your world saves normally.
